text:
alex: Hey @people-ops — heads up I'm starting a domestic adoption (placement expected mid-May). Quick Qs: what's the paid leave policy for adoption, is there an adoption/legal stipend, what docs do you need, and can I do a phased return (0.6 FTE) for ~6 weeks?

anna (People Ops): Congrats @alex! Short answers: Redwood provides up to 12 weeks fully paid parental leave for primary caregivers (applies to adoption & foster placements). We also offer a one-time adoption reimbursement stipend up to $3,000 for eligible expenses (legal fees, travel, placement costs). For paperwork we need either the adoption decree or placement agreement + itemized receipts uploaded to the HRIS within 60 days of placement. Phased return is supported with manager sign-off — we usually do a 4–8 week ramp (0.5–0.8 FTE). I'll DM you the checklist and the form link. :tada:

hr-bot: Required docs (upload to HRIS -> Documents > Leaves): 1) placement_agreement or adoption_decree, 2) itemized_receipts.pdf, 3) completed_stipend_form.pdf. File naming convention example:
```
alex_adoption_2026-05_decree.pdf
alex_adoption_2026-05_receipts.zip
```
Please allow HRIS validation (48–72 hrs) and then approval workflow.

sara (eng manager): @alex we can make the phased return work. Tentative approval for 0.6 FTE first 6 weeks, then reassess. Please put proposed dates in the shared leave calendar and cc me. I'll coordinate sprint coverage.

ben (Payroll): Stipend note: once docs are approved in HRIS we process reimbursement on the next monthly payroll cycle. Typical turnaround is ~2 pay cycles from approval. If you need an advance for urgent travel, ping payroll@redwood (we'll evaluate case-by-case).

alex: Thanks — one more: can I stack 2 weeks vacation before placement so the 12 weeks push later, or does vacation count against leave?

anna (People Ops): You can absolutely use vacation days before or after leave to stagger time off. Vacation does not reduce your 12-week paid parental leave entitlement, but payments will be sequenced (vacation pay first, then parental pay). Add tentative dates to the leave calendar so payroll and benefits can align.

sara (eng manager): I'll draft a coverage plan for the sprint. @mike can you pick up code reviews and on-call for weeks 20–22?

mike: Yep I got reviews and on-call. :thumbsup:

alex: Are there differences for international adoption (visas, extra travel time)?

anna (People Ops): For international adoption we still cover the 12 weeks and the $3,000 stipend. We also offer an additional unpaid travel extension up to 2 weeks in cases of visa delays and access to a travel concierge vendor (for flight/hotel rebooking). We'll schedule a 30-min call to walk through timelines and required immigration paperwork.

anna (People Ops): Links/resources I'll share: HRIS leave guide (link in DM), stipend request form (link), sample coverage template (in People Ops drive). I'll follow up in DM with the checklist and the exact upload path. If anyone else has practical tips for adoption timing logistics please chime in. :seedling:
